summary: M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1970 to 1980. McCabe later held an academic post at King's College London from circa 1990 to 2014 and taught Amber D. Carpenter.

M. N. Srinivas worked in Indology, studying at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai under G. S. Ghurye, and the University of Oxford. Srinivas held posts at Baroda College, the University of Delhi, and founded and chaired the Institute for Social and Economic Change.

M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Calicut, Varier also served there from circa 1973 to 1996 as a Reader in Epigraphy and taught Francis N. J.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Mysore from circa 1951 to 1955, Rao served as Director of the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage from circa 1972 to 1983.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 1899, Sastri is attested as Curator of the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University, Kolkata.
M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied at Agoura High School, Art Center College of Design, and under teacher Seiren Matsunami.

Mabel Haynes Bode worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying under Cecil Bendall, T. W. Rhys Davids, and Eduard Müller-Hess at the University of Bern. Bode held posts at University College London (~1912–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).
Madan Mohan Malaviya was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1880–1884) and the University of Allahabad (~1891–1893). Malaviya also founded Banaras Hindu University.

Madeleine Biardeau was an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar educated at École normale supérieure de jeunes filles (~1942–1946). Biardeau taught at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989), where students included Greg Bailey and Jacques Scheuer.
Madhav Krishna Sharma was an Indology scholar who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1952, Sharma served as an Inspector for the Department of Sanskrit Education, Rajasthan.

Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indology and linguistics scholar who served as a Professor at the University of Michigan, attested in 1976 and 2006–2009. Deshpande taught Jonathan A. Silk, Hyoung Seok Ham, C. W. Huntington, and David Fiordalis.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. In 2012, Khanna held attested posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhukar Anant Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist who served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983).

Madhusudan Dhaky was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Fergusson College from circa 1945 to 1949. Dhaky held posts at the American Institute of Indian Studies, including Associate Director (~1976–1996).

Mae Chee Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master Degree of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong served as thesis advisers.

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who taught Liu Shi. Deokar held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021).

Maheshachandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. Bhattacharyya served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, attested in 1882 and 1914.

Mahinda Deegalle studied at Harvard Divinity School and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds, Wendy Doniger, and Diana L. Eck. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Deegalle held posts at Bath Spa University, Harvard, and Colgate University.
Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Otani University (~2003–2008). In 2010, Iuchi held an attested post at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.
Mai Mishiro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Mishiro held an attested post with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2011 and an attested post at Waseda University in 2016.
